newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia palm oil ends lower after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia palm oil ends lower after choppy session.

text.p: PALMOIL FUTURES PALMOIL PHYSICALS
Nov (3rd pos) 1,209 rgt/tonne Sep (south) 1,235 *
Open/hi/low 1,230/1,236/1,205 Prev close 1,245
Prev settlement 1,232 * sellers prices

PALMOIL FUTURES - Prices end choppy session lower on profit-taking. May consolidate further before resuming uptrend. Near-term outlook encouraging due to good export demand. Immediate support seen at 1,200 ringgit.
PALMOIL PHYSICALS - Also weakened but ended off day's lows. Trades again mainly on crude palm oil.
Malaysian palm oil futures prices ended a choppy session lower as players locked in profits after recent sharp advances, dealers said.
"The market rebounded strongly in early afternoon trade but fell back on heavy profit-taking," said one trader.
Traders said some retracement has been expected as prices had risen more than 80 ringgit over the past two weeks to reach three-month highs on Tuesday.
They said a pullback would be healthy for the market as near-term prospects remain encouraging on the back of strong export demand.

On Tuesday, India's State Trading Corporation bought 12,000 tonnes of palm olein for September/October shipment while Trading Corporation of Pakistan took 6,000 tonnes RBD palm oil and 3,000 tonnes palm olein for October 10 delivery.

Industry officials in India have said the country might import up to 250,000 tonnes of palm olein during the Hindu festival months of September and October to offset thin domestic supplies. Most of the oil is likely to come from Malaysia as Indonesia, another leading exporter, is facing tight domestic supply, traders said.
Traders said further consolidation was likely before the market could resume its uptrend.

Benchmark third position Nov crude palm oil futures closed at 1,209 ringgit ($484.96) a tonne, down 23 ringgit, after trading in a range of 1,205-1,236. Traders expect immediate support for the contract at 1,200 ringgit.
Total turnover on the futures market fell to 2,580 lots against 4,711 lots on Tuesday.
Physical prices also weakened but losses were smaller compared with those on the futures market.
Sep (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,235 ringgit ($495.39) a tonne with bids at 1,225. It was last traded at 1,235 ringgit.
Sep (central) was offered at 1,220 with bids at 1,205, and Sep (north) saw offers at 1,205 and bids at 1,195.
Oct (south) was offered at 1,240 ringgit with bids at 1,230, after trading between 1,240 and 1,250.
Oct (central) saw offers at 1,225 ringgit and bids at 1,210, and Nov (south) at 1,250 against 1,235.
Among refined products, Sep RBD palm olein was offered at $575 a tonne, FOB Malaysia, Oct at $565 and Nov/Dec at $557.50. Oct was traded at $562.50 and Nov/Dec at $555.
Sep and Oct RBD palm oil were offered at $530 and Nov/Dec at $527.50.
Sep RBD palm stearin saw sellers at $415, Oct at $420 and Nov/Dec at $425. Sep was done at $410.
Sep/Oct palm fatty acid distillate was offered at $332.50.
